
This checks if v[i] >= v[k] for all k < i. So it's checking if v[i] is a "left-to-right maximum" (the maximum so far including position i).

And peekSum sums up v[i-1] when isPeek(v, i-1) is true. So it's summing up all the left-to-right maxima.

Now in the method, the algorithm tracks `lmax` which is the maximum of v[0..i-1]. When v[i] >= lmax, it adds v[i] to sum and updates lmax. This correctly identifies the left-to-right maxima.

The issue is whether the verifier can prove this. The invariants are:
1. `lmax in v[..i]` - lmax is some element in the first i elements
2. `forall k:: 0<=k<i ==> lmax>=v[k]` - lmax is the max of v[0..i-1]
3. `sum==peekSum(v, i)` - the main invariant

peekSum(v, i+1) = v[i] + peekSum(v, i) [when isPeek(v, i) is true]
